The sprint's own commits and every code path are silent. The executor flagged it and left MS3 passes=false instead of editing the frozen design; the controller should trim the fence when it lands the doc. Classified non-blocking because the false element is not a defect of the sprint under review, no behaviour or guard is affected, and the remedy is a landing-time documentation edit.

The guard has no comment or string awareness: a wrong pair mentioned in a comment ('## {"index": 1, "id": "CNS5:3627"}') or held inside a single-quoted Python string ('{"index": 1, "id": "CNS5:1676"}') is flagged as a mismatch. It fails closed, so it is not vacuous, but prose or JSON-in-a-string would need a SOURCE_EXEMPT row.

Blind spots, all documented in the design's Risks and none a regression of this sprint: a dictionary written entirely in single-quoted Python literals is not matched; only tracked files are scanned, so a brand-new file is invisible until it is added (CI sees it once committed); GDScript &"..."/^"...", variables and field-by-field dictionaries are out of reach.

The sprint plan's M3 expectation is mis-stated: replacing every \s* with one space still matches the tree's one-space literals, so it kills 1 control, not the 3 the plan predicted. The shipped matcher is in fact whitespace-tolerant (verified). The executor flagged the deviation instead of editing the plan - the inaccuracy is in the plan, not in the code.

The sprint JSON is still status 'planned' with evaluations {} and pr null and no milestone completion timestamps, and the design doc is still marked 'Planned' under design_docs/planned/. These are the controller's landing steps (rubric phase 3.5), so they are pre-landing state rather than defects, but they must be closed before landing.
